```text
1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We formalized recursive generation depth estimation and showed that 19 statistical features achieve 70--85\% four-class accuracy ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$; cross-model 66.4\%, cross-strategy 59.1\%).
5	Future work should address wild-data transfer, larger scales, and strategy-conditioned classifiers; code and data will be released upon acceptance.
6	
7	\section*{Limitations}
8	\label{sec:limitations}
9	
10	\paragraph{Cross-strategy deployment constraint.}
11	Cross-strategy transfer induces a d1/d2 boundary inversion under temperature sampling.
12	Per-strategy z-score normalization partially corrects the inversion (GPT-2~XL d1v2 AUC $0.24{\to}0.56$, OLMo $0.19{\to}0.70$) but leaves a residual gap relative to within-strategy performance (${\sim}0.83$), indicating that a two-stage pipeline (strategy identification + strategy-conditioned classification) is needed for reliable cross-strategy deployment.
13	
14	\paragraph{d0 inflation of headline metrics.}
15	Depth~0 (human-written text) is near-perfectly separable (recall $>$98\% across all settings), inflating headline accuracy.
16	Cross-model transfer accuracy of 66.4\% is substantially driven by d0; d2 recall drops to 26.8\% in the worst case (Pythia holdout).
17	
18	\paragraph{Controlled vs.\ ecological setting.}
19	All experiments use Wikipedia seed text with controlled recursive generation (LoRA fine-tuning, 1--1.5B parameter models).
20	Transfer to mixed-domain corpora, instruction-tuned models, and larger scales (7B+) remains open.
21	Wild-data calibration is probed only indirectly; ecological transfer is future work.
22	
23	\paragraph{EDD monotonicity assumption.}
24	Our EDD definition (Eq.~\ref{eq:edd}) requires all pairwise AUCs up to depth $d^*$ to exceed $T$, which is well-behaved when AUC decays monotonically---as observed in all our configurations.
25	However, \citet{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement} show that early recursion can temporarily \emph{improve} model quality, which could produce non-monotonic AUC profiles (e.g., a dip at d1/d2 followed by recovery at d2/d3).
26	Our cross-strategy transfer results provide an empirical example: training on nucleus + top-$k$ and testing on temperature yields d1-vs-d2 AUC as low as 0.129 (GPT-2~XL) and 0.253 (OLMo), violating the monotonicity assumption.
27	In such cases EDD would conservatively report a lower value than the deepest discriminable pair, potentially underestimating the true discriminable range; extending EDD to handle non-contiguous discriminable regions is future work.
28	The choice of threshold $T$ is also application-dependent: at $T{=}0.80$, several cells lose one depth level relative to $T{=}0.75$.
29	
30	\paragraph{Reference model dependency.}
31	Surprisal-based features are computed relative to GPT-2 base (124M), introducing partial overlap when GPT-2~XL is held out, though GPT-2~XL holdout accuracy (67.6\%) does not exceed the unrelated OLMo (69.2\%).
32	The choice of reference model affects feature values; a different reference model may shift absolute feature magnitudes and potentially alter discriminability at depth boundaries.
33	
34	\paragraph{Additional caveats.}
35	Detection features degrade under domain shift \cite{pudasaini2026_detection_fails}; our depth features are likely susceptible.
36	\citet{falahati2026_curated} show that curated synthetic data need not trigger collapse, attenuating the fingerprints we exploit.
37	
38	\section*{Ethics Statement}
39	
40	This work uses publicly available pretrained language models (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2~XL) and Wikipedia text as seed data.
41	No human subjects were involved, no private or sensitive data were collected, and no new models were released.
42	Our method is intended to support data provenance and training-data auditing; we acknowledge that depth estimation tools could in principle be misused to circumvent content moderation, though such risks are shared with all detection-oriented research.
```

```text
1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	Predicted depth can serve as a quality proxy for importance weighting \cite{dsir2023,qurating2024}, down-weighting deeply recursive samples that binary filters \cite{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse} would discard indiscriminately.
5	The residual gap after per-strategy normalization (\S\ref{sec:gen:crossstrategy}) motivates a two-stage pipeline of strategy identification followed by strategy-conditioned classification.
6	Real-world documents may interleave segments at different recursion depths, requiring extension to segment-level estimation.
7	Adversarial paraphrasing \cite{sadasivan2023_paraphrase} could disrupt the statistical fingerprints we exploit; combining depth estimation with watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} and model attribution \cite{uchendu2020_attribution} could form a unified provenance toolkit.
8	Scaling to larger models (7B+) and deeper recursion ($d{>}5$) remains open.
9	
```

    "originalFile": "\\section{Conclusion}\n\\label{sec:conclusion}\n\nWe formalized recursive generation depth estimation and showed that 19 statistical features achieve 70--85\\% four-class accuracy ($\\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$; cross-model 66.4\\%, cross-strategy 59.1\\%).\nFuture work should address wild-data transfer, larger scales, and strategy-conditioned classifiers; code and data will be released upon acceptance.\n\n\\section*{Limitations}\n\\label{sec:limitations}\n\n\\paragraph{Cross-strategy deployment constraint.}\nCross-strategy transfer induces a d1/d2 boundary inversion under temperature sampling.\nPer-strategy z-score normalization partially corrects the inversion (GPT-2~XL d1v2 AUC $0.24{\\to}0.56$, OLMo $0.19{\\to}0.70$) but leaves a residual gap relative to within-strategy performance (${\\sim}0.83$), indicating that a two-stage pipeline (strategy identification + strategy-conditioned classification) is needed for reliable cross-strategy deployment.\n\n\\paragraph{d0 inflation of headline metrics.}\nDepth~0 (human-written text) is near-perfectly separable (recall $>$98\\% across all settings), inflating headline accuracy.\nCross-model transfer accuracy of 66.4\\% is substantially driven by d0; d2 recall drops to 26.8\\% in the worst case (Pythia holdout).\n\n\\paragraph{Controlled vs.\\ ecological setting.}\nAll experiments use Wikipedia seed text with controlled recursive generation (LoRA fine-tuning, 1--1.5B parameter models).\nTransfer to mixed-domain corpora, instruction-tuned models, and larger scales (7B+) remains open.\nWild-data calibration is probed only indirectly; ecological transfer is future work.\n\n\\paragraph{EDD monotonicity assumption.}\nOur EDD definition (Eq.~\\ref{eq:edd}) requires all pairwise AUCs up to depth $d^*$ to exceed $T$, which is well-behaved when AUC decays monotonically---as observed in all our configurations.\nHowever, \\citet{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement} show that early recursion can temporarily \\emph{improve} model quality, which could produce non-monotonic AUC profiles (e.g., a dip at d1/d2 followed by recovery at d2/d3).\nOur cross-strategy transfer results provide an empirical example: training on nucleus + top-$k$ and testing on temperature yields d1-vs-d2 AUC as low as 0.129 (GPT-2~XL) and 0.253 (OLMo), violating the monotonicity assumption.\nIn such cases EDD would conservatively report a lower value than the deepest discriminable pair, potentially underestimating the true discriminable range; extending EDD to handle non-contiguous discriminable regions is future work.\nThe choice of threshold $T$ is also application-dependent: at $T{=}0.80$, several cells lose one depth level relative to $T{=}0.75$.\n\n\\paragraph{Reference model dependency.}\nSurprisal-based features are computed relative to GPT-2 base (124M), introducing partial overlap when GPT-2~XL is held out, though GPT-2~XL holdout accuracy (67.6\\%) does not exceed the unrelated OLMo (69.2\\%).\nThe choice of reference model affects feature values; a different reference model may shift absolute feature magnitudes and potentially alter discriminability at depth boundaries.\n\n\\paragraph{Additional caveats.}\nDetection features degrade under domain shift \\cite{pudasaini2026_detection_fails}; our depth features are likely susceptible.\n\\citet{falahati2026_curated} show that curated synthetic data need not trigger collapse, attenuating the fingerprints we exploit.\n\n\\section*{Ethics Statement}\n\nThis work uses publicly available pretrained language models (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2~XL) and Wikipedia text as seed data.\nNo human subjects were involved, no private or sensitive data were collected, and no new models were released.\nOur method is intended to support data provenance and training-data auditing; we acknowledge that depth estimation tools could in principle be misused to circumvent content moderation, though such risks are shared with all detection-oriented research.",

    "originalFile": "\\section{Generalization and Robustness}\n\\label{sec:generalization}\n\nWe test whether the atlas results (69.6--85.4\\%) reflect genuine statistical regularities or training artifacts, evaluating four axes: classifier choice (\\S\\ref{sec:gen:baselines}), cross-model transfer (\\S\\ref{sec:gen:crossmodel}), cross-strategy transfer (\\S\\ref{sec:gen:crossstrategy}), and end-to-end learning (\\S\\ref{sec:gen:e2e}).\n\n\\subsection{Baseline Comparison}\n\\label{sec:gen:baselines}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:baselines} compares classification methods on the Pythia-1.4B nucleus setting.\nThree feature-based methods---Random Forest (RF), CORAL ordinal regression \\cite{coral2020}, and DivEye \\cite{diveye2026}---all operate on the same 19 statistical features and achieve statistically indistinguishable accuracy (78.1--78.2\\%; pairwise bootstrap $p>0.05$ after Bonferroni correction, 95\\% CI within $\\pm$1.1pp).\nThese three significantly outperform CE-MLP ($p<0.001$, $+$3.8pp), which in turn trails logistic regression by $\\sim$0.1pp.\nSingle-feature regression on mean perplexity performs at chance (25.1\\%), confirming that depth estimation requires the multi-dimensional feature representation defined in \\S\\ref{sec:method}.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Comparison of classification methods on Pythia-1.4B nucleus.
